cards.text: Twenty YEARS, friend. That's how long Solomon, king of Israel, spent building two houses: the house of the LORD and his royal palace. Now he has something for Hiram king of Tyre, the man who supplied him with cedar and cypress logs and gold for his every desire.

cards.question: Solomon gives Hiram king of Tyre twenty ___ in the land of Galilee.

cards.text: So Hiram goes out from Tyre to inspect his twenty new towns. Then he asks Solomon, “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?”

cards.question: Hiram is pleased with the twenty towns Solomon gave him.

cards.text: He is NOT pleased, and he calls them the Land of Cabul, a name they still had when this was written. That's a man who opened the cookie box and found crumbs.
Oh, and Hiram had sent the king 120 talents of gold. Back when I lived in a junk drawer, the richest thing in there was an expired coupon.

Next comes the account of the forced labor behind Solomon's building: the LORD's house, his palace, the wall of Jerusalem, towns like Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer, and store cities for his chariots and horses. About Gezer: Pharaoh king of Egypt had captured it, set it on fire and killed the Canaanites living there. Then he gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife.

That's a LOT of building. And still living in the land are people who aren't Israelites, the ones the Israelites were unable to devote to destruction: Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.

cards.question: Who does Solomon conscript to be his forced laborers?

answers.text: The non-Israelites still in the land

cards.question: Solomon has all those chariots and horses, but he doesn't consign a single Israelite to slavery. Why not?

answers.text: They are his men of war and commanders
They pay Solomon a yearly tax
They are needed to farm the land

cards.question: On Solomon's projects, the Israelites are also the chief ___: 550 supervisors over the people who do the work.
As soon as Pharaoh's daughter comes up from the City of David to the palace Solomon built for her, Solomon builds the supporting ___.

cards.text: Three times a year, Solomon offers burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he built for the LORD, burning incense with them before the LORD. So he completes the temple.

cards.question: King Solomon assembles a fleet of ships at Ezion-geber, near Eloth in Edom, on the shore of the Red Sea. Who sends servants, sailors who know the sea, to serve in the fleet?
Hiram's sailors and Solomon's servants set sail together. Where do they go to bring back gold?

cards.text: They bring back 420 talents of gold from Ophir and deliver it to Solomon.
